summary.title: OCCAMS Dataset
summary.abstract: A clinically linked multi-omic dataset containing 500 matched tumour-normal pairs from patients with early to advanced oesophageal and junctional adenocarcinoma[cite: 4]. Sourced from 27 UK centres, the dataset integrates longitudinal clinical data with whole-genome sequencing, bulk RNAseq, and methylation array profiles[cite: 4].

documentation.description:
The OCCAMS dataset is a comprehensive, clinically linked multi-omic resource containing data from 500 patients with early to advanced oesophageal and junctional adenocarcinoma recruited across 27 UK centres[cite: 4]. It provides longitudinal clinical tracking—with up to 10 years of survival data—paired with standardized whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic, and epigenomic profiles to facilitate deep molecular and clinical research[cite: 4].

### Dataset Overview & Demographics
- **Geography:** Patients recruited from 27 centres across the UK[cite: 4].
- **Clinical Indications:** Early to advanced oesophageal adenocarcinoma and junctional adenocarcinoma[cite: 4].
- **Patient Volume:** 500 patients providing matched tumour-normal sample pairs[cite: 4].
- **Sex Distribution:** 85% Male, 15% Female[cite: 4].
- **Clinical Pathway Details:** Cohort reflects approximately 4,300 patients treated with standard of care, including radiotherapy, chemotherapy, endoscopic therapy, and surgery (oesophagectomy)[cite: 4].

### Curated Clinical Data Scope
- **Baseline & Demographics:** Captures patient gender, age at diagnosis, date of diagnosis, comorbidities, TNM tumour stage (at diagnosis and pre-treatment), histology, and tumour site[cite: 4].
- **Treatment & Response:** Documents treatments given, start dates, number of cycles, total dose, treatment protocol, Mandard score for tumour response, and date of surgery[cite: 4].
- **Recurrence & Survival:** Tracks date and site of recurrence, and provides follow-up survival data for up to 10 years, cross-checked with the Office for National Statistics (ONS)[cite: 4].
- **Exposures & Family History:** Includes smoker status, medication usage, and reflux history[cite: 4].

### Multi-Omic Profiling & Sample Types
- **Genomics (500 pairs):** Whole genome sequencing of matched tumour-normal pairs using Illumina NGS technology[cite: 4]. Reference samples sequenced to 30x depth and tumour samples to 50x depth[cite: 4]. Covers variant calls, SNVs, indels, SVs, CNAs, mutational signature exposures, and tumour mutational burden (Held in VCF, BEDPE, or CSV format)[cite: 4].
- **Transcriptomics (300 pairs):** Bulk RNAseq sequenced via Illumina NGS[cite: 4]. RNA reads are quantified with TPM values calculated (Held in TXT format)[cite: 4].
- **Epigenetics (285 pairs):** Methylation array data generated via Illumina’s MethylationEPIC BeadChip technology (Held in IDAT format)[cite: 4].
- **ctDNA Samples:** Approximately 750 whole blood samples suitable for ctDNA analysis, with longitudinal samples available[cite: 4].
- **Sample Collection:** Primary tumour resections (prioritizing pre-treatment endoscopic biopsies or post-treatment surgical resections), matched normal tissue, and germline blood samples[cite: 4]. Collected at multiple timepoints where possible (pre-chemotherapy, at surgery, post-surgery, post-chemotherapy)[cite: 4].
- **Standardization:** All sequencing data is processed and managed at the CRUK Cambridge Institute using QC tools like FASTQC and Picard[cite: 4].

### Data Access Governance & Licensing
- **Commercial Rights:** Cancer Research Horizons (CRH) holds exclusive commercial rights to the dataset[cite: 4].
- **Licensing Terms:** Access is granted on a non-exclusive basis solely for the approved purpose via time-limited licences (typically a 3-year term)[cite: 4].
- **IP Ownership:** Any IP generated from using the data will be owned by the company, unless used in collaboration with CRH[cite: 4].
- **Access Mechanism:** Access to sequencing reads is facilitated through the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA), while access to variants and quantification may be provided via a separate server[cite: 4].
- **Application Process:** Companies must submit a data access request to CRH outlining the proposed study, intended use (technical and lay terms), required data types/subsets, and potential patient benefit[cite: 4]. Applications are reviewed by the OCCAMS Data Access Committee[cite: 4].
